definitions_and_hypotheses_checked: General n, compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth M, actual flow on [a,b], a<b; only the raw filling-area and sphere-family part specializes to dimension three.

Smooth-interior M62 solutions differ from jointly C1, spatially C2 M63 solutions. Intrinsic regularity does not smooth arbitrary original labels. Endpoint value/velocity/curvature live in actual tangent bundles.
Rm(A,B,C,D)=g(R(A,B)D,C); horizontal H differs from (H,1); spatial and spacetime normal derivative squares differ by Q(S,H)^2.
C0=2K0+6K2+2K2^2+6K1 and C1=C0/2. Regularization divides by positive h_epsilon. Theta has an integral and epsilon/delta forward estimate, not a claimed derivative at zeros.

The slope equation is unconditional but the Ricci lower estimate is sign-guarded. Positive slope implies positive degree. The forced quotient retains C1/u and depends on initial minimum slope for fixed circumference.

Uniform length/turning hypotheses are imposed at a, not s, on an existing full-interval curve. Every subarc of at most one period is quantified. No ramp hypothesis. Curvature includes the upper endpoint; higher jets use a strictly interior window; both exclude s.
Full D_s^iH is used. The concrete radius0 is one; delta=delta0*radius0^2 is retained. Ambient derivative constants precede circumference and curve.
Flattening is a homeomorphism, not a diffeomorphism. Horizontal coefficient is side speed. Constant base sides remain immersed graphs.

Raw approximation works at every positive tolerance, while one older public field restricts tolerance<1. A continuous family of smooth loops does not mean smooth dependence on the sphere parameter. No joint continuity in circumference is claimed.

source_comparison: MT2007 Claim 19.22 printed p. 452 calls the horizontal coefficient L a side length. With cell length 2*pi/N and the actual profile normalization the coefficient must be constant side speed. The chapter uses the actual Lean velocity and verifies its integral.

MT2007 Lemmas 19.24 and 19.58 include the restart time in an interval displaying 1/(t-s). The actual estimates and chapter exclude that time, preserving the separate closed upper endpoint for the curvature cap.
The 2015 correction adds initial-length dependence, linear curvature forcing and the C1/u quotient source. These are retained throughout.
The current local C2 construction, fixed-label endpoint recovery and finite weighted comparison are developed from workspace sources. This is source-specific reconstruction, not a novelty claim.
